title: ESOP Tax Rules for ITR: Navigating Salary & Capital Gains
description: ESOPs are taxed at two distinct stages: when you exercise them and when you sell the shares. The difference between the Fair Market Value (FMV) on exercise da.

faq.q: What is the Fair Market Value (FMV) for ESOPs?
faq.a: The FMV is the market price of the share on the date you exercise your options. For listed shares, it's typically the average of opening and closing prices on the stock exchange. For unlisted shares, it's determined by a SEBI-registered merchant banker.

Tax on the perquisite (salary income) at exercise is due in the financial year you exercise the options, usually deducted as TDS by your employer. Tax on capital gains from selling the shares is due in the financial year you sell them.

For unlisted company ESOPs, the Income Tax Act provides for deferment of TDS on perquisite income to the earlier of: 48 months from the end of the relevant assessment year, date of sale of shares, or date of cessation of employment.

faq.q: How do NRIs pay ESOP tax?
faq.a: NRIs are subject to Indian tax laws for income accrued or arising in India. The perquisite income from ESOPs exercised while working in India or for an Indian company is taxable in India. Capital gains from the sale of shares of an Indian company are also taxable in India.

faq.q: Which ITR form should I use for ESOPs?
faq.a: If you have only salary and ESOP perquisite income, ITR-1 might suffice. However, if you have capital gains from selling ESOP shares, you will typically need to file ITR-2 or ITR-3, depending on your other income sources.

faq.q: Is STT (Securities Transaction Tax) applicable to ESOPs?
faq.a: STT is applicable only when you sell listed shares on a recognised stock exchange. It is not applicable at the time of exercising your ESOPs or for unlisted shares.

faq.q: What if my company is delisted after I exercise ESOPs?
faq.a: If your company delists after you exercise but before you sell, the shares become unlisted. Any subsequent sale will be treated as capital gains from unlisted shares, affecting the holding period for LTCG and the tax rate.
